Subject: Request: temporary throughput variance for Dedicated capacity

Hi Ben,

We’re seeing a sustained increase in peak inference volume on our Dedicated pool (payment-processing scoring routes) that will run for the first three weeks of June. Our ops team is reporting periodic queueing for high-priority routes during the 09:00–11:00 and 16:30–18:30 windows PST.

Can Redwood provide a time‑boxed throughput variance or temporary headroom on our reserved GPUs for June 1–21? Specifically, we are asking for ~2x effective throughput during those 2-hour windows or an equivalent queueing carveout so latency stays within our P95 target of 220ms.

I’ve attached a short snapshot of our request and recent logs (quantum_sla_snapshot.pdf) and a CSV with sample queueing spikes. Let me know what information you need to evaluate this. We’re open to short-term fees if necessary — priority is reliability for our live customers.

Thanks,
Lisa Tanner

Quantum Holdings

Ben / Marissa — dug into their logs (see queueing_analysis.csv) and did an infra sanity check. Short answer: yes, we can offer a controlled, time-boxed throughput variance, but there are constraints. Notes: 

- Reserved GPUs enforce committed concurrency and isolated slices. We can’t change the hard limit on the reservation without reconfiguration, but we can provide additional burst capacity from a shared headroom pool that effectively increases throughput for selected tenant routes.
- Burst pool: limited and billed; we can guarantee additional capacity during scheduled windows if Quantum commits to: (a) schedule windows in advance (48h notice), (b) tag the high-priority routes, and (c) accept an automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model or reduced concurrency if pre-warm fails.
- Queueing policy: we can implement a route-level priority that routes payment-scoring requests to the burst pool during windows. This reduces cross-tenant impact but requires warmed KV cache and model-variant pinning. Warm-up typically takes ~20–30 minutes for their model topology.
- Monitoring: we’ll add route-level SLO dashboards and a one-click rollback. We should define a hard cap (e.g., +40% throughput during windows) rather than 2x to be conservative and avoid impacting other customers.

Recommendations for the addendum: 30‑day trial (June 1–21), +40% guaranteed throughput during scheduled windows, 48h notice for scheduling, explicit fallback to model-variant with documented behavior, and a usage-based surcharge. I attached the CSV and a short analysis.

If legal signs off, I can provide the technical text for the addendum and an ops runbook.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed time-boxed throughput addendum (draft) — Quantum Holdings

Hi Lisa — thanks for your patience. Per our internal review we can support a time-limited throughput variance under the following terms (high level):

1) Scope: Dedicated SKU (Quantum Holdings reserved pool) — payment-scoring routes only.
2) Term: June 1–21, 2027 (30 calendar days).
3) Guarantee: Additional headroom equal to up to +40% throughput during scheduled windows (09:00–11:00 & 16:30–18:30 PST) subject to burst pool availability.
4) Preconditions: 48 hours’ advanced schedule for each window; pre-warm period of 30 minutes prior to each window; tagging of routes and model-variant pinning.
5) Fallback: If pre-warm fails or headroom is exhausted, traffic will automatically fall back to the committed reserved capacity or a compatible model-variant.
6) Fees: usage-based surcharge for burst pool consumption (we’ll bill for actual burst tokens + a standing $X/day premium during the term).
7) Monitoring: Route-level SLO dashboards, alerting, and a one-click rollback.

I’ve attached a draft addendum (redwood_draft_addendum.pdf) and linked a DocuSign for review: https://www.docusign.net/transaction/qh-2027-568-addendum. If you’re good with the high-level terms we’ll push this to Legal for a short-form addendum and coordinate an ops dry-run (pre-warm) the day before the term begins.

Let me know if Quantum needs a stricter P95 guarantee — that will require a different commitment level and an expanded fee.

—Ben
Ben Carter
